newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: Sao Tome's Trovoada sworn in for second term.
newsitem.headline: Sao Tome's Trovoada sworn in for second term.

text.p: President Miguel Trovoada was sworn in on Tuesday for a second five-year term as president of the West African twin island state of Sao Tome and Principe, officials said.
In his acceptance speech, Trovoada urged Sao Tomeans to adopt "a spirit of dialogue, tolerance and mutual respect" to resolve the country's problems.
The ceremony was attended by dignitaries including Cape Verde President Mascarenhas Monteiro, Guinea-Bissau President Joao Bernardo Vieira and Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama.
Trovoada won 52.74 percent of the vote and his rival Manuel Pinto da Costa took 47.25 percent in a second round run-off on July 21, according to official figures from the Supreme Court.
Abstention among the electorate of 50,000 was around 20 percent, officials said.
Sao Tome and Principe, a former Portuguese colony located 125 miles (200 km) off Gabon, is one of the poorest countries in the world.
